programme.title: Live NFL
programme.desc: Detroit Lions v Chicago Bears (Kick-off 6.00pm). Coverage of the week 12 match from Ford Field. The Lions have played a home game on Thanksgiving Day almost every year since 1934, with the only exceptions being six years during World War II. The tradition began when then-owner George A. Richards wanted to build excitement and draw attention ahead of a match against the unbeaten Chicago Bears, and it proved to be so successful it was broadcast by 94 radio stations across the country, becoming the first-ever national NFL radio broadcast.

programme.title: Live NFL
programme.desc: Dallas Cowboys v Philadelphia Eagles (Kick-off 9.30pm). Coverage of the week 12 match from AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. The Cowboys first played a Thanksgiving Day fixture in 1966 and have done so every year since then, except for 1975 and 1977. They come into this year's match having won in each of the last three years, including a 31-28 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs 12 months ago.

programme.title: Live NFL
programme.desc: Buffalo Bills v Kansas City Chiefs (Kick-off 1.20am). Coverage of the week 12 match from Highmark Stadium, as the longtime rivals face each other on Thanksgiving Day for the very first time. While the rivalry between these teams dates back to the 1960s and the AFL days, it has risen to national prominence as both teams have consistently contended for the AFC title following the emergence of quarterbacks Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, who have featured in every game between the teams since 2020.

programme.title: The Price Is Right
programme.desc: "Come on down!" "The Price Is Right" -- hosted by Bob Barker until 2007 and Drew Carey thereafter -- features a wide variety of games and contests with the same basic challenge: Guess the prices of everyday (or not-quite-everyday) retail items. Four contestants, all of whom are seated in one of the wildest audiences in daytime game-show history, are called to the stage to play a preliminary pricing round. That winner joins the host on stage for one of more than 70 different pricing games. After three such games, the contestants spin a big wheel -- hoping to get as close to $1 as possible -- in the "Showcase Showdown." The two highest winners of that round advance to the final, where prizes could be cars or roomsful of furniture. A trio of models presents the prizes.

programme.title: Let's Make a Deal
programme.desc: CBS adds to its daytime game-show lineup with an updated version of the classic TV show of the 1960s, filmed in Los Angeles. Hosted by comic/singer/actor Wayne Brady, contestants -- often dressed in a wide variety of original costumes -- will still compete for money and prizes by striking wacky deals. Jonathan Mangum is the show's announcer, and Monty Hall, arguably the best-known host of the earlier version of the show, is listed among the new show's creative consultants. The program won a Daytime Creative Arts Emmy Award for Outstanding Original Song in 2014 for "30,000 Reasons to Love Me," composed by Cat Gray and performed by Wayne Brady.
